root_cause.text: The `claimed` and retune control flags in `struct mmc_host` were defined as bitfields sharing the same memory word, causing non-atomic read-modify-write (RMW) operations to concurrently overwrite each other in asynchronous contexts.
root_cause.evidence: The commit message states that "The host->claimed bit shared a word with retune flags. Writes to claimed in __mmc_claim_host() or retune_now in mmc_mq_queue_rq() can overwrite other bits when concurrent updates happen in other contexts", and the patch diff replaces the `claimed:1`, `can_retune:1`, `retune_now:1`, and `retune_paused:1` bitfields with independent `bool` variables.

unsigned int		can_retune:1;	/* re-tuning can be used */

unsigned int		retune_now:1;	/* do re-tuning at next req */
unsigned int		retune_paused:1; /* re-tuning is temporarily disabled */
